Data is fresh, not stale.

reaction.trapRisk: SMH volume ran 1.99x its 20-day average with no intraday reversal and VIX is at its 5-day high, so any bounce into the SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH 580-600 failure zone is a bull trap until it holds. Entries wait for the retest verdict or a second low that holds with the 10-year falling — never chase the first bounce.

strategyPosture: Watch. SPX sits 5.96% below its 200-day, SMH and NVDA are both below Zone 2, VIX is at its 5-day high of 35.89, and the capitulation tally is 1 of 4 — there is no floor to buy into and no confirmed bottom to deploy against. Hold existing positions; any selling happens on strength days, never after a break.

themes.counterRead: Price and fundamentals are moving in opposite directions across the whole AI supply chain — that is the setup the conviction engine is flagging (NVDA score 83, AVGO 80, LRCX 81). But the tape has no floor: SMH at $400.06 and NVDA at $125.53 are both BELOW Zone 2 ($470-505 / $175-185), and the mechanical capitulation tally is 1 of 4. Fundamentals ahead of price is an opportunity only once a floor forms; until then it is a watchlist, not an entry.

themes.watchFor: SMH closing back above $470 and NVDA above $175, with the capitulation tally reaching 3 of 4.

themes.counterRead: Rotation is the correct label for now, but it is not a comfort read: the divergence is real and credit conditions can flip. If lending standards tighten while the Mag 7 gap widens, rotation becomes rollover. The index-level decline (-11.91% from the 120-day high) masks that the pain is concentrated in the names that dominate index weight.
themes.dataAnchor: The weakness is concentrated, not broad: Mag 7 names average 24.97% below their 52-week highs versus SPY 11.7% — a 13.27-point divergence gap. NVDA is the weakest Mag 7 name at 48.4% below its high; AAPL is the strongest at just 5.1% below. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% (SLOOS), far below the ~40% stress threshold. SPY itself is down 8.7% over one month while QQQ is down 12.31% — the growth leadership is what is breaking, not the broad market.
themes.label: Concentration Unwind: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The index is falling, so the read is that the whole market is rolling over — the Mag 7 leadership that carried the index is breaking.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS lending standards rising toward 40% or the Mag 7 / SPY divergence gap widening past 20 points.

themes.counterRead: The equity break without a credit break is what keeps this a CORRECTION-class episode rather than a confirmed regime break — but the spread is widening steadily (3.20% on Nov 12 to 3.52% now), not calm and flat. Credit is the tripwire: it is the one signal that has not fired, and the one that would change the stance fastest.
themes.dataAnchor: Credit has not confirmed it. HY OAS is 3.52%, still below the 4.00% stand-down line, and the episode block marks credit calm=true, cracking=false — the only confirmed leg of the 1-of-4 mechanical tally. Rates are orderly: 10Y at 5.04%, 2Y at 4.76%, curve 2s10s +0.28 (not inverted), real 10Y 2.89%, DFF 3.88%. No AI borrower has defaulted in the data.
themes.label: Credit Calm While Equities Break
themes.narrative: A 8.61% five-day SPX drop, VIX at 35.89 (+85.96% in five days), and a seventh straight down day read as a credit event in the making.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4.00% — the stand-down / regime-break line.

themes.counterRead: Leverage magnifies a correction into a wipeout — a 3x daily-reset product falling 35% in a month needs a ~55% gain just to get back. The narrative that the leveraged tail is 'cheap' is ahead of any evidence of a bottom: no VIX rollover, no volume climax reversal, no zone reclaim. The holdings list carries TQQQ, CONL, DOGE and BMNR — this is where the portfolio damage is concentrated, and where patience costs least.
themes.dataAnchor: TQQQ is down 35.64% over one month and 12.77% today; CONL is down 65.54% over one month and 11.83% today. BMNR is down 40.44% over one month, 11.08% today, about $1 above its $12.80 52-week low. ETH is down 25.7% over one month (though +3.36% today) and BTC down 23.11%. None of these has a floor: TQQQ's own framework has no buy condition until $54 is reclaimed with the watcher gate, and BMNR's add condition is ETH reclaiming $1,800 and holding.
themes.label: Leveraged Tail: The Dip-Buying Narrative Has No Floor

themes.watchFor: TQQQ reclaiming $54 with the watcher gate, or ETH reclaiming $1,800 and holding it.
